title: Ines and the Sigil
premise: Orsen Vane, a mercenary whose god went silent five years ago, survives by selling outlawed charms in the city of Corvane until prayers across the country begin to be answered again — and her sigil burns back to life, marking her as both miracle and target. Hunted by the Ministry of Silence and courted by factions who want to weaponize the returning gods, she discovers the gods never left: they were imprisoned beneath the country's drowned heart, and their waking is tearing reality open. To escape, Orsen must reach the Door of Ash, the last exit from a nation that officially no longer exists, and choose between sealing the gods away forever or freeing them at the cost of her own identity as their sworn blade. She frees them, surrendering her sigil and her power, and walks out of the dying country nameless but finally belonging to herself.
about_author: Juniper Okafor is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing banned texts in West African university libraries before turning to fiction full-time. She writes fantasy about faith, borders, and the people history forgets to record.

chapters.title: Charms for a Silent God
chapters.summary: Orsen Vane sells a luck-charm to a frightened fisherman in outlawed Corvane, hiding her dead god's sigil beneath her sleeve. A Ministry sweep nearly catches her; an old contact, Tallow, warns that prayers are being answered somewhere north. POV: Orsen. Beat: weary survival, first crack of hope.

chapters.title: The Prayer That Answered Back
chapters.summary: A desperate woman begs Orsen for a healing charm for her son; when Orsen marks it, the sigil flares with real power for the first time in five years — and the boy lives. Word spreads overnight. POV: Orsen. Beat: terror and wonder tangled together.

chapters.title: Ministry of Silence
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Halvard Rell interrogates Orsen about the miracle, revealing the Ministry has known about returning divinity for weeks and is executing 'vessels.' He lets her go — as bait. POV: Orsen, with a cold interlude from Rell. Beat: hunted, paranoia takes root.

chapters.title: Tallow's Map
chapters.summary: Tallow reveals a smugglers' route to the Door of Ash, the only way out of the country the Treaty dissolved on paper. He wants passage money Orsen doesn't have; she agrees to one last job: escort a pilgrim caravan north. POV: Orsen. Beat: reluctant commitment, fragile alliance.

chapters.title: The Pilgrim Road
chapters.summary: On the road, Orsen meets Sefa, a blind girl who hears the gods speaking and claims one of them is calling Orsen by her true name — a name Orsen buried with her old life. POV: alternating Orsen and Sefa. Beat: unease deepening into dread and longing.

chapters.title: What the River Remembers
chapters.summary: The caravan crosses a river where the drowned capital once stood; the water shows visions of the gods' imprisonment five years ago — and Orsen sees her own past self among those who chained them. POV: Orsen. Beat: guilt surfaces; her identity cracks open.

chapters.title: Ashes of the Congregation
chapters.summary: They find a village of worshippers massacred by Ministry purges, one survivor raving that the gods are screaming underground. Rell's riders arrive; the caravan scatters. POV: Sefa. Beat: horror, loss of innocence, stakes made flesh.

chapters.title: Bargain at the Waystation
chapters.summary: Trapped in a mountain waystation during the first snows, Orsen bargains with a renegade Ministry defector, Yara, who offers safe passage in exchange for the sigil itself. Orsen refuses. POV: Orsen. Beat: temptation and defiance; power's price named aloud.

chapters.title: The God Beneath the Snow
chapters.summary: Avalanche buries the pass; in the white silence Orsen meets her silent god face to face in a dream — he is not dead but starving, imprisoned, and he begs her not to free him. POV: Orsen. Beat: revelation inverted; fear of what rescue would mean.

chapters.title: Sefa's Sermon
chapters.summary: Sefa preaches to frozen survivors that the gods' return is mercy, gathering a following that includes some of Orsen's escorts. Orsen watches her own legend being built without her consent. POV: Sefa. Beat: power corrupting through devotion, even gentle devotion.

chapters.title: Rell's Offer
chapters.summary: Rell corners Orsen alone: the Ministry will spare the pilgrims if she surrenders the sigil and names the other vessels. He shows her files proving she helped imprison the gods five years ago. POV: Orsen. Beat: betrayal of self; the past weaponized.

chapters.title: The Name I Buried
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: five years earlier, Orsen — then called Vessa, blade-sworn of the god Ossuin — drove the binding-stake herself, believing she was saving the world. POV: Orsen/Vessa. Beat: devastating self-recognition; she is the prison's architect.

chapters.title: Fracture
chapters.summary: The caravan learns of Orsen's past from Rell's propaganda leaflets; Sefa's followers turn on her, and Yara abandons them. Tallow dies holding the pass so the rest can flee. POV: Orsen. Beat: belonging shattered; lowest point begins.

chapters.title: Winter's Long Fall
chapters.summary: The group, reduced to Orsen, Sefa, and two others, treks through a land where winter falls unnaturally fast — the imprisoned gods' death throes freezing the country from below. POV: Sefa. Beat: apocalyptic dread; the world ending quietly.

chapters.title: The Drowned Heart
chapters.summary: Guided by Sefa's hearing, they descend into the sunken capital where the gods are bound. Orsen sees all seven, and understands freeing them means unmaking the binding — and the part of herself forged by it. POV: Orsen. Beat: awe and terrible clarity.

chapters.title: Rell's Last Sermon
chapters.summary: Rell arrives with Ministry forces, revealing his true aim: not to destroy the gods but to bind them to himself as the new state church's living weapons. Battle erupts in the dark halls. POV: Rell, then Orsen. Beat: corruption of power made explicit; climax ignites.

chapters.title: The Stake and the Hand
chapters.summary: In the chaos, only Orsen can pull the binding-stake — it answers to its maker. Sefa urges freedom; the god Ossuin, freed enough to speak, offers her power instead if she leaves him bound and rules beside him. POV: Orsen. Beat: the final temptation; everything hinges on choice.

chapters.title: Door of Ash
chapters.summary: Orsen chooses neither throne nor silence: she pulls the stake, freeing the gods, as Rell's forces and the collapsing prison come down around them. The Door of Ash opens in the ruin — exit for mortals only. POV: Orsen. Beat: climax resolved through sacrifice of self.

chapters.title: Nameless
chapters.summary: Crossing the Door, Orsen loses the sigil, her god-given strength, and the name Vessa entirely — emerging on the far border as no one at all, while behind her the gods rise over a thawing land. POV: Orsen. Beat: grief and liberation indivisible.

chapters.title: The Country That No Longer Exists
chapters.summary: Refugees stream out through the Door into a borderland camp; Sefa becomes a voice for the freed gods' gentler worship, and asks Orsen to stay and help lead. POV: Sefa. Beat: new belonging offered — but on Orsen's terms now.

chapters.title: Small Charms, Honestly Sold
chapters.summary: Spring. Orsen keeps a stall at the camp market selling honest charms with no god behind them, visited by travelers who knew her legend and see only a tired woman mending luck. POV: Orsen. Beat: quiet reclamation of ordinary life.

chapters.title: Ines
chapters.summary: Asked her name at last by a child buying a charm, Orsen gives the one her mother used before any god claimed her: Ines. She walks into the thawing world belonging to no one and herself. POV: Orsen. Beat: resolution — identity chosen, not granted.
